steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A good essay has: introduction, 3-4 developed paragraphs, conclusion

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The introduction should define key terms and indicate your line of argument

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Use PEEL: Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link back to the question

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Evidence must be specific — named characters, events, sources and cultural details

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What does PEEL stand for? | Q: What should an introduction include? | Q: Why is a conclusion essential?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link — ensures each paragraph is focused and developed. | Definition of key terms, understanding of the question, and indication of your line of argument. | Without a conclusion delivering a justified judgement, you cannot access the top mark band.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Spend 2-3 minutes planning before writing Start each paragraph with a clear topic sentence Use specific named evidence from the classical world In your conclusion, make a clear definitive judgement If running out of time, write a brief conclusion rather than none
